text:
Hi,

My contract with Birkenrain Trading Ltd says that, once the trial period is over, either side has to give three months' notice to the end of a month. I specifically asked for that when I signed, because I was leaving a safe job. It's far longer than the one month you'd normally get in the first year.

Now they've given me notice anyway. On 9 June 2026 Anna Moser, the sales director, called me into a meeting room in St. Gallen and handed me a letter saying my employment was being terminated. She said the sales figures in my region were 'not where they should be'. My colleague Ian Weber was let go the same week.

The trial period is the part that confuses me. The contract also sets its own trial period, not the usual one month, that I'm sure of. But the probation clause is on page 2, which I lent to Ian last week so he could compare it with his, and I can't remember the exact wording any more.

I've attached page 1 of the contract, with the start date and the notice clause.

I earn CHF 3,350 a month. When does my job actually end, and what do I do if they try to pay me for less?

Thanks,
Peter Baumann
Schulhausstrasse 58, St. Gallen

EMPLOYMENT CONTRACT - page 1

between
Birkenrain Trading Ltd, St. Gallen, represented by Anna Moser, Sales Director (employer)
and
Peter Baumann, Schulhausstrasse 58, 9000 St. Gallen (employee)

1. Start of employment
The employment begins on 23 March 2026 and is concluded for an unlimited period.

2. Position
Sales representative, region Eastern Switzerland, full-time.

3. Salary
CHF 3,350 gross per month plus commission according to annex.

4. Notice period
After the probation period, the employment may be terminated by either party with three months' notice to the end of a calendar month.

(continued on page 2)
